items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public health law and the education law, in relation to
including certain pharmacists as qualified health care professionals and
authorizing such pharmacists to complete a waived test
items.lawCode: Amd §§571, 579 & 206, Pub Health L; amd §6801, Ed L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3467

SPONSOR: RIVERA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law and the education law, in relation
to including certain pharmacists as qualified health care professionals
and authorizing such pharmacists to complete a waived test

 
PURPOSE:

The bill adds pharmacists to the list of licensed healthcare profes-
sionals authorized under the public health law to perform non-invasive
laboratory tests, as specified in regulations issued by the Commissioner
of Health, as an adjunct to their professional services.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends paragraph 6 of section 571 of the Public Health Law,
regarding Clinical Laboratory and Blood Banking Services, to include
pharmacists on the list of licensed healthcare professionals who are
qualified to perform clinical laboratory tests that do not use an inva-
sive modality.

Section 2 of the bill amends subdivision 1 of section 579 of the Public
Health Law, pertaining to scope and exceptions, to exempt clinical labo-
ratories operated by the federal government and blood banks operated by
pharmacists, consistent with the limitations to be established in subdi-
vision (w) of section 206 of this chapter.

Section 3 adds a new subdivision 9 to section 6801 of the Education Law,
pertaining to the definition of practice of pharmacy, to expand the
scope of practice for a licensed pharmacist to perform a "waived test."

Section 4 adds a new paragraph (w) to section 206 of the Public Health
Law, pertaining to the duties of the commissioner, to authorize the
Commissioner to establish the list of Clinical Laboratory Improvement
Amendments (CLIA)-waived tests that pharmacists may perform and estab-
lish the requirements for pharmacists reporting test results to primary
care physicians.

Section 5 establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

New York needs to catch up to the rest of the country concerning the
scope of practice for pharmacists. According to the National Association
of the Boards of Pharmacy, 39 states currently permit pharmacists to
perform non-invasive FDA-approved tests, commonly described as Clinical
Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)-waived tests.  These are
simple, low-risk tests available without a prescription or medical
order.

Pharmacists are licensed clinicians uniquely situated to advance New
York's public health objectives as they represent an opportunity to
engage members of the public that otherwise might not be reached.
Authorizing the Commissioner of Health to specify the tests that a phar-
macist would perform limits the actual tests to be completed by pharma-

cists and provides needed flexibility to respond to public health needs
and programs.

This legislation can improve therapeutic outcomes and the quality of
care overall. As mentioned, pharmacists are well-positioned to enhance
the continuity of care connected to a patient's medical home.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: S5092/A3867A McDonald

2021-2022: S2529 Rivera/A3033 McDonald

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately, provided that amendments subject
to expiration and reversion take effect and the addition or repeal
necessary for the implementation of this act are authorized to be made
and completed before effective.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3467A

SPONSOR: RIVERA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to allowing a licensed
pharmacist to order and administer certain tests; and to amend part C of
chapter 57 of the laws of 2022 amending the public health law and the
education law relating to allowing pharmacists to direct limited service
laboratories and order and administer COVID-19 and influenza tests and
modernizing nurse practitioners, in relation to the effectiveness there-
of

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to expand pharmacists' ability to perform
tests for certain illnesses and conditions to also include respiratory
syncytial virus (RSV), strep throat, HbA1c (blood sugar levels), hepati-
tis C (Hep C), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivision 7 of section 6801 of the Education Law, as
it relates to the definition of the practice of pharmacy, to allow a
licensed pharmacist to perform limited service laboratory and ordering
and administering a test for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), pharyn-
gitis resulting from group A streptococcal infection (commonly referred
to as strep throat), HbA1c (blood sugar levels), hepatitis C, and human
immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

Currently under this section of law pharmacists are already authorized
to initiate tests for COVID-19 and influenza.

Section 2 extends the effective date of the underlying section of law
that authorizes pharmacists to order and administer tests by an addi-
tional two years until April 1, 2026.

Section 3 establishes an effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

New York State is behind the rest of the country concerning the scope of
practice for pharmacists and health care in general, especially when it
comes to collaborative practice.

According to the National Association of the Boards of Pharmacy, 39
states currently permit pharmacists to Perform non-invasive FDA-approved
tests, commonly described as Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments
(CLIA)-waived tests. These are simple, low-risk tests available without
a prescription or medical order.  During the COVID-19 pandemic and
beyond, pharmacists were a valuable community service provider for COVID
testing and it makes sense to expand testing in a limited manner to
other disease states such as RSV, strep throat, Hep C, and HIV for
patient convenience. The bill would also allow a pharmacist to test
HbA1c, a common test for blood sugar levels associated with diabetes.

Pharmacists are licensed clinicians uniquely situated to advance New
York's public health objectives as they represent an opportunity to
engage members of the public that otherwise might not be reached.
Authorizing the Commissioner of Health to specify the tests that a phar-
macist would perform limits the actual tests to be completed by pharma-
cists and provides needed flexibility to respond to public health needs
and programs.

This legislation can improve therapeutic outcomes and the quality of
care overall. As mentioned, pharmacists are well-positioned to enhance
the continuity of care connected to a patient's medical home.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: S5092/A3867A McDonald - Advanced to Third Reading

2021-2022: S2529 Rivera/A3033 McDonald - Advanced to Third Reading

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
